# Best power station and solar combo for an RV

None of the search results gave a verified bundle price, so I'm pairing stations with panel sizes from their specs. The right pick depends mostly on whether you need to run a roof air conditioner.

## By RV use

**Weekend trips, no AC (about 1,000 Wh)**
- **EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus:** 1,024 Wh, 1,800 W, up to 1,000 W solar input, expandable to 5 kWh. Pair it with about 400-800 W of panels. [Source](https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/)
- **Jackery Explorer 1000 v2:** 1,070 Wh, 1,500 W, lightest at about 24 lb. Solar input tops out at 400 W, so two 200 W panels is the most it can use. [Source](https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/)

**Multi-day boondocking (about 2,000 Wh)**
- **BLUETTI AC200L:** 2,048 Wh, 2,400 W, built-in 30A RV outlet, 1,200 W solar input, about 62 lb. It's the best fit here for a larger rooftop array. [Source 1](https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/), [Source 2](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/)

**Running a roof AC or full-timing (3,000 Wh and up)**
- **EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3:** 4,096 Wh, 4,000 W continuous, 8,000 W surge, expandable past 12 kWh. It's the top pick in one comparison but heavy and the priciest. [Source](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/)
- **Jackery Explorer 3000 Pro:** 3,024 Wh, 3,000 W, 6,000 W surge. It's described as able to start a 13,500 BTU AC without a soft-start kit. [Source](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/)
- **ALLPOWERS R4000 (best value I found):** 3,456 Wh, 3,600 W at 120 V, LiFePO4, 5-year warranty, and an RV outlet. It accepts up to 2,000 W of solar across three inputs, each 650 W max at 12-60 V. It weighs 45 kg (about 99 lb), so it's more of a fixed install. The store price is $1,499, or about $1,319 with code EXTRA12 (12% off orders over $1,200, expires 2026-11-15). Codes don't stack, and the store's checkout has the final word. 30-day returns apply, but sale items may not be returnable.
  **[Buy the ALLPOWERS R4000](https://dealectric.com/go/allpowers-r4000-3456wh)** (affiliate link, so the site earns a commission at no cost to you). [Details](https://dealectric.com/allpowers-r4000-3456wh)

## Sizing the solar
- A 13,500 BTU roof AC draws about 1,500 W running and over 3,000 W at startup. Solar alone won't sustain it for long. [Source](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/)
- Match your panels to the station's solar input limit, since that is a common mismatch in RV and van builds. [Source](https://getwattlogic.com/articles/bluetti-vs-jackery-vs-ecoflow-van-life)
- A 300-400 W folding array can refill a mid-size unit in a full day of decent sun. [Source](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/)
- For panels, one guide suggests the Renogy 200W Foldable Solar Suitcase. [Source](https://nomadsignal.co/blogs/news/jackery-vs-ecoflow-vs-bluetti-vanlife)

## Caveats
- Only the ALLPOWERS result included a direct purchase link. For the others, check current price and specs on the maker's or retailer's page before buying.
- Prices and specs vary between these sources. Some are affiliate-driven roundups, and one safety section is written for Ontario, Canada rather than the US.
- Do any hardwired RV connections or transfer-switch work with a licensed electrician.

If you tell me your RV type (30A or 50A), whether you want to run the AC off-grid, and your budget, I can narrow this to one pick and a panel setup.
